items.title: Section: Can Ordinary Meditators Really Transform Matter, or Only Buddhas and Advanced Bodhisattvas?

items.zh: 又定所行色，若依此繫定，即由此繫大種所造。又此定色但是世間，有漏、無漏由定而生，非出世間。由此定色，有戲論行定為因故。又非一切所有定心皆有能生此色功能，唯一類有如能起化。謂不思惟，但由先時作意所引，離諸闇昧，極善清淨明了現前，當知是定乃能生色。若定力勵數數思惟，假勝解力而得見者，當知不能生起此色。又復此色，雖非出世定之所行，然由彼定增上力故，有一能現。當知此事不可思議。
items.en: Meditatively mastered matter, depending on whichever realm the meditation belongs to, is produced by that realm's own elements. This meditative matter is only worldly, either contaminated or uncontaminated depending on the meditation, not supramundane, since it has conceptual, deliberate meditation as its cause. Not every meditative mind has the capacity to produce this matter — only one particular kind does, namely one that, without present deliberation, but simply through prior intention, free of all obscuration, extremely pure and clearly manifest, is capable of producing matter. If, through effortful, repeated deliberation and borrowed conviction, something is merely seen, one should know this cannot produce such matter. And although this matter is not the domain of supramundane meditation, through that meditation's own superior power, some are able to manifest it — one should know this is inconceivable.

items.zh: 問：欲、色二界實物有色，何差別耶？

items.title: Section: Six Marks of Form — Own-Nature, Shared Nature, Mutual Dependence, and the Four Elements' Own Distinct Functions

items.zh: 答：色界諸色清淨最勝，能發光明。又極微細，下地諸根所不行故。又無有苦，依彼諸色苦受不生故。欲界不爾。是名差別。復次，色蘊略由六相應知。一、自相，二、共相，三、能依所依相屬相，四、受用相，五、業相，六、微細相。自相者，謂地等以堅等為相，眼等以各別清淨色為相。共相者，謂一切色皆變礙相。能依所依相屬相者，大種為所依，造色是能依。受用相者，為內色處有所受用增上力故，外色境界差別而生。或有色聚唯有堅生，或唯有濕、或唯有煗、或唯有動、或和合生，為欲隨順內諸色處受用差別故。業相者，謂地等諸大種，以依持、攝受、成熟、增長為相。
items.en:
Answer: form-realm matter is pure and supreme, able to emit light. It is also extremely subtle, beyond the reach of lower faculties. And it has no suffering, since painful sensation does not arise depending on it. The desire realm is not so. This is the distinction.
Furthermore, form aggregate should be known by six marks in brief: own-nature, shared nature, mutual-dependence nature, function-of-use, function, and subtlety.
Own-nature is earth and the rest having solidity and so on as their mark, and the sense faculties each having their own particular pure matter as their mark. Shared nature is all form having the mark of change and obstruction. Mutual-dependence nature is the elements being what is depended upon, derived matter being what depends upon them. Function-of-use is derived matter arising in accordance with the internal sense faculties' need to make use of it, so that external objects arise with corresponding differences. Function is the elements having support, gathering, ripening, and growth as their marks.

items.title: Section: Interpenetrating Bodies of Light, a Boy Who Ran Through Glass Unharmed, and Kumārajīva's Bell — Kind's Closing Mark

items.zh: 微細相者，謂極微相。復次，微細性略有三種。一、損減微細性，二、種類微細性，三、心自在轉微細性。損減微細性者，謂分析諸色至最細位，名曰極微。種類微細性者，謂風等色及中有色。心自在轉微細性者，謂色、無色二界諸色。如經說：有等心諸天，曾於人中如是如是資熏磨瑩其心；隨此修力，住一毛端空量地處，展轉更互不相妨礙。如是等輩，應當思惟觀察色蘊物類差別。
items.en:
Subtlety is the mark of the subtlest particle. Furthermore, subtlety is briefly of three kinds: subtlety through reduction, subtlety of category, and subtlety through mental mastery. Subtlety through reduction is analysing form down to its finest position, called the subtlest particle. Subtlety of category is such things as wind and the matter of the intermediate state. Subtlety through mental mastery is the matter belonging to the form and formless realms.
As the scripture says: certain devas of equal mind, having while among humans cultivated and refined their minds in just this way, by the power of this cultivation dwell upon a space no larger than the tip of a hair, passing through one another without any mutual obstruction. Beings such as these should be contemplated and observed regarding form aggregate's distinctions of kind.

items.title: Section: Five Ways Particles Are Established, and Why Clustering Matter Still Counts as Obstructive

items.zh: 問：諸極微色，由幾種相建立應知？答：略說由五種相。若廣建立，如本地分。何等為五？一、由分別故；二、由差別故；三、由獨立故；四、由助伴故；五、由無分故。分別建立者，謂由分別覺慧，分析諸色至極邊際，建立極微；非由體有。是故極微無生無滅，亦非色聚集極微成。差別建立者，略說極微有十五種。謂眼等根有五極微，色等境界亦五極微，地等極微復有四種，法處所攝實物有色極微有一。獨立建立者，謂事極微，建立自相故。助伴建立者，謂聚極微。所以者何？於一地等極微處所，有餘極微，同聚一處，不相捨離，是故依此立聚極微。問：何因緣故，諸有對法同處一處，不相捨離，而不說名無對性耶？答：隨順轉故。由彼展轉相隨順生，不相妨礙。又由如是種類之業增上所感如是而生。何以故？一切色聚，一切色根共受用故。若異此者，一切聚中，非有一切地等諸色不相捨離。若爾，眼等諸識境界便不遍滿一切聚中，如是應無遍滿受用。是故當知，定有諸色同一處所，不相捨離。
items.en:
Question: by how many marks should the subtlest particles of matter be known to be established? Answer: briefly, by five marks... first, through analysis; second, through category; third, through independence; fourth, through companionship; fifth, through indivisibility.
Established through analysis: by analytical understanding breaking matter down to its finest limit, the particle is established — not through any actual essence. Hence the particle neither arises nor ceases, nor is any cluster of matter formed by particles accumulating.
Established through category: briefly, there are fifteen kinds of particle — five for the sense faculties, five for their objects, four for the elements, and one for genuinely real matter subsumed under the mental sense-field.
One should therefore know that various forms of matter definitely occupy the same location without ever abandoning one another.

items.zh: 又有諸色，或於是處互相妨礙，或於是處不相妨礙，如中有色等。而彼諸色非無對性。此中道理，當知亦爾。無分建立極微者，謂非彼極微更有餘分，非聚性故。諸聚極微可有細分，若極微處即唯此處，更無細分可以分析。

blocks.text: Can meditation produce matter? The treatise says yes, within limits. Then it explains "particles": not tiny solid things, but the limit of analysis.

This form is only worldly, since it has absorption with conceptual activity as its cause. Only one kind of absorption can produce it: "drawn by prior intention, free of obscuration, extremely pure and clear". Master Cháng Bǎi: before entering, one first intends what to manifest. Through the transmundane absorption's superior power, some can also manifest it; the treatise calls this inconceivable.

Pure and luminous, extremely subtle, and free of suffering. Master Cháng Bǎi: outer things exist according to beings' use of them; they appear to suit the needs of the body that uses them. (Untranslated, 0597b20: "How do the real forms of the desire and form realms differ?")

By reduction (the particle reached by analysis), by category (wind and intermediate-state matter), and by mastery of mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: one with absorption is no longer bound by desire and can manifest forms freely. Devas dwelling on a hair-tip do not obstruct one another; Master Cháng Bǎi, ordinary beings discriminate large and small, self and other, and so obstruct each other.
Particles are established by analysis, "not through any actual essence". Master Cháng Bǎi: having no substance, what arising or ceasing could a particle have?
"Ordinary beings discriminate large and small, and so obstruct each other." Master Cháng Bǎi turns physics into a lesson about the mind.

quiz.q: Is the form of absorption worldly or supramundane, and why?
options: only worldly, whether contaminated or uncontaminated according to the absorption, since its cause is an absorption with conceptual activity
supramundane, since only noble ones can manifest it and ordinary beings cannot, so it is not worldly
neither worldly nor supramundane, for it is inconceivable
supramundane, because it arises from unconditioned suchness
quiz.why: The treatise says this form is only worldly, contaminated or uncontaminated according to the absorption, since it has absorption with conceptual activity as its cause. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is produced in absorption by ordinary and noble ones through conviction based on verbal proliferation, and so is worldly, not the realm of the ultimate. Ordinary beings manifest contaminated form, noble ones uncontaminated form.

quiz.q: What kind of meditative mind can produce this form?
options: one that strives, deliberating repeatedly, and sees by the power of conviction
every meditative mind produces it, the capacity coming with entry into any absorption, however shallow
only supramundane absorption, never a worldly one
one that, without deliberation, is drawn by prior intention, free of obscuration, extremely pure and clear
quiz.why: The treatise says only one kind of absorption can do this: without present deliberation, drawn by prior intention, free of obscuration, extremely pure and clear. Master Cháng Bǎi: before entering absorption one first intends to manifest thus; if one must strive and deliberate, relying on the force of conviction, one cannot manifest such form.

quiz.q: This form is not the domain of supramundane absorption, yet some can manifest it through its power. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: this is a contradiction in the treatise; the two cannot both stand, the former prevails and the latter may be struck
"some" means the Buddha alone, no other noble one being able
through the dominant force of uncontaminated absorption it can arise without contaminated absorption as cause
supramundane absorption directly takes this form as its object
quiz.why: The treatise says that although this form is not the domain of supramundane absorption, through that absorption's superior power some can manifest it, and calls this inconceivable. Master Cháng Bǎi: it can arise through the dominant force of uncontaminated absorption, without an absorption with conceptual activity, that is, contaminated absorption, as its cause.

quiz.q: How does form-realm matter differ from that of the desire realm?
options: pure and supreme, able to emit light; extremely subtle, beyond lower faculties; without suffering, painful feeling not arising from it
coarser, obstructing lower levels; it has painful feeling, though lighter than below
unable to shine, relying on sun and moon; seen by lower faculties as desire-realm matter is, and differing only in length of life
provisional, not real, and so without any function
quiz.why: The treatise gives three differences: form-realm matter is pure and supreme and emits light; it is extremely subtle, beyond the reach of lower faculties; and it has no suffering. Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodies of form-realm gods do not fall ill, so they have no painful feeling; and if such a god wishes to be seen by desire-realm humans, they manifest something coarser.

quiz.q: The English has "Function-of-use is derived matter arising ...". Compared with the Chinese, how does the subject differ, and what of the term?
options: the Chinese subject is outer objects, differing by the use of inner faculties; the English says derived matter, and "function-of-use" sits too close to "function"
the Chinese subject is the inner faculties, with outer objects as users; the English swaps them, wholly reversing the direction
the Chinese subject is the four elements, rendered as derived matter
the Chinese subject is the store-consciousness, wholly omitted
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: outer objects exist according to beings' use of them, and that use is not apart from this thought; these differing forms appear in order to accord with the inner body's need to use them. The Chinese subject is outer objects. The English "derived matter" is an addition, though defensible, and "function-of-use" beside "function" blurs 受用 and 業.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of subtlety?
options: through reduction, matter of the form and formless realms; of category, analysis to the particle; through mental mastery, wind and intermediate-state matter
through reduction, analysing form to the particle; of category, wind and intermediate-state matter; through mental mastery, matter of the form and formless realms
through reduction, a wasting body; of category, the five faculties; through mental mastery, the mental faculty
all three mean the particle, being three names with no difference in content
quiz.why: The treatise lists subtlety through reduction, the particle reached by analysis; of category, wind and intermediate-state matter; and through mental mastery, form and formless matter. Master Cháng Bǎi: intermediate-state form is very subtle, seen only by the purest divine eye. Those with absorption, he adds, manifest forms at will through conviction.

quiz.q: Why does form of those in absorption belong to subtlety through mental mastery?
options: because their bodies have been analysed down to particles, and so are invisible to the eye
because they are unaffected by the elements, need no support, and require no working of the mind
because they are all reborn in the formless realm
the mind, no longer bound by desire, turns freely and manifests forms through conviction
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind of one with absorption is no longer bound by desire and can turn freely; it can manifest various forms according to its conviction. So the subtlety here lies in mastery of mind, not in small size, which is the first kind of subtlety.

quiz.q: Devas of equal mind dwell on a hair-tip without obstruction. What does Master Cháng Bǎi draw from this?
options: the obstruction of form is the mind's own discrimination; without it there is no obstruction
the gods' bodies are so tiny that they fit, which is a matter of size and not of the mind's cultivation
a hair-tip is in fact vast, though ordinary beings cannot tell
this is only a figure, the treatise not holding it to be so
quiz.why: The treatise cites a scripture on devas dwelling on a hair-tip's space without mutual obstruction. Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary beings discriminate forms as large or small, self or other, the mind unequal, and so obstruct one another; the obstruction of these forms is the discrimination of one's own mind, and without discrimination there is none.

quiz.q: By what five marks does the treatise say particles are established?
options: earth, water, fire, wind, and space
analysis, category, independence, companionship, and indivisibility
reduction, category, mental mastery, resistant, and non-resistant, set by differences of subtlety and obstruction
colour, sound, smell, taste, and touch
quiz.why: The treatise lists analysis, category, independence, companionship, and indivisibility. Master Cháng Bǎi on the third: establishing the own-mark of a particular form-thing through its particular particle is establishment through independence. The English gives only part of this passage; much of the treatment of the last three marks is untranslated.

quiz.q: Why is the particle without arising or ceasing, and why establish it at all?
options: the particle is the most durable real thing, and so neither arises nor ceases; it explains how the world is built up from it
it is set up by analysis and has no substance, so has no arising or ceasing; it is established to free beings from attachment to form
only buddhas see the particle, and ordinary beings do not, so they call it unarising, though it really does arise
the particle does arise and cease, "none" being a manner of speaking
quiz.why: The treatise says analytical understanding breaks matter down to its limit and so establishes the particle, not through any actual essence. Master Cháng Bǎi: having no substance, what arising or ceasing could it have? To meet people's needs, particles are spoken of, so that beings may lose attachment to form. It is a tool for contemplation, not a building block.
